resources.string: Tapo account, energy tariff and privacy
Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening TapoCtrl.
TapoCtrl only talks to devices on your home network. It never contacts TP-Link or any other server, and has no analytics or tracking.
The PIN can\'t be recovered. TapoCtrl will forget your Tapo account hashes and your device list, reset its settings and turn the app lock off. Your plugs and bulbs themselves aren\'t changed.
Add your Tapo plugs and bulbs by their address, or scan your Wi-Fi network for them.
That isn\'t an address on your home network. TapoCtrl only connects to private addresses such as 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x.
No answer. Is the device plugged in and on the same Wi-Fi as this phone?
This device doesn\'t accept your Tapo account; check the email and password under Tapo account.
Enter your Tapo account first, so TapoCtrl can talk to this device.
This device uses older firmware TapoCtrl doesn\'t support yet. Updating its firmware may help.
This device is already in your list.
Nothing answered at %1$s. Check the address and that the device is on.
You\'ll find the address in your router\'s list of connected devices. Giving the device a fixed address there keeps it the same.
Connect this phone to your Wi-Fi to scan.

The scan asks every address on this phone\'s Wi-Fi subnet whether it\'s a Tapo device, and sends TP-Link\'s local discovery broadcast. Nothing about your account is sent and nothing leaves your network.
Devices on another network or a guest Wi-Fi can\'t be found from here
Your devices only answer to the account they were set up with. Enter it once; it stays on this phone.

Your plugs and bulbs check the Tapo account they were set up with. Enter its email and password once. TapoCtrl turns them into the two hashes the devices check, keeps only those, and forgets the password.
To change the account (for example after changing your Tapo password), enter it again.
As hashes only, encrypted with a key in the phone\'s secure hardware
Neither your email nor your password is stored.
Couldn\'t save the account. Try again.
TapoCtrl never sends your email or password anywhere: not to TP-Link, not to any server. Only your own devices on this network see a hash of them, during their encrypted handshake.
TapoCtrl deletes the saved hashes and their key. Your devices keep working, but TapoCtrl can\'t control them until you enter the account again.
Measured by the plug. Costs are an estimate from your tariff in Settings.
Measured by the plug. Set your electricity price in Settings to see an estimated cost.
Model, firmware, MAC address and signal
TapoCtrl stops showing it. The device keeps its settings and stays on your Wi-Fi; you can add it again any time.
The device reports that it\'s too hot
KLAP, encrypted, on your local network

The device asks TP-Link itself whether there\'s a newer version and downloads TP-Link\'s signed firmware on its own. TapoCtrl only tells it to check and to install; it never handles the firmware file.
This device is up to date.
TP-Link gave no release notes for this version.

The device downloads version %1$s from TP-Link and restarts. While it restarts, a plug briefly cuts power to whatever is plugged into it, and a bulb goes off for a moment. It may take a few minutes. Don\'t unplug it.
Don\'t unplug the device. Leaving this page doesn\'t stop the update.
Updated. The device now runs version %1$s.
The device restarted and reports version %1$s. If that\'s still the old version, check again in a few minutes.
The device hasn\'t answered for 15 minutes. Check that it\'s plugged in, then open it again.
Used to estimate what plugs that measure energy (such as the P110 and P115) cost today and this month.
Today, 7 days, 30 days and 12 months, from the plug\'s own memory
The plug has no energy recorded for this period yet.
Energy use, %1$s: %2$s in all. Tap a bar for its value.
Read from the plug\'s own energy memory, on your network. Reading it never switches the plug or changes anything on it. Hours and days follow the plug\'s clock.
